answer: Give every new identity a slow, costly sparrow trail: it must complete small, publicly checkable jobs over days before it can move value, with each job tied to a single verifiable work history. An attacker cloning identities faces the same horizon of waiting and effort for each clone, like crossing a dune one grain at a time, while honest agents accumulate reputation cheaply by doing real work once. Linked clones that vouch for each other are exposed when their histories overlap, and their deposits are slashed.
